findings.text: Upheld as advisory. The throw in levelRefusal guards a pair (local, allowed) that effectiveLevel never makes, so no production path can reach it (question 9). The reviewer itself says it is no defect, because it makes a broken rule loud instead of hiding it. Suggestion: carry the rule in the type and say in decide's doc that it can throw.
Upheld as advisory. A one-line duplicate of rootOf in src/sharing/report.ts:159 (question 2). The rubric treats a one-line duplicate as advisory.
Upheld as advisory, carried from round three. Nothing reads the fileList and ignored fields of EffectiveShareList, and fileListsOf parses the env file a second time (questions 2 and 8).
Upheld as advisory, carried from round three. Only tests import the GENERATION_KEY and newGeneration re-exports, and REBIND is exported but used only in its own file (question 8).
Upheld as advisory, carried from round three. policyWith is test-only and exported from a production module (question 8).
Upheld as advisory, carried from round three. The two sharing key names are declared again in several places although settings.ts exports SHARING_KEYS (question 2, boilerplate).

Upheld as advisory, carried from round three. listProjects repeats entryAliases' remote:% alias query and its isHostLedAlias filter (question 2). The finding names a function in the diff but no line number, and an advisory needs no line.
Upheld as advisory, carried from round three. The resolvePaths().dataDir fallback is used only by older tests; both production callers pass dataDir (question 9).

Raised as a defect, lowered to advisory. The rule for this gate: a ui-ux defect is upheld only when it cites evidence inside review/ that review/ui-evidence.json lists (no such file exists), or review/design-lint.json, or a diff line that a capture cannot show, with the reason. This finding cites review/ui/manifest.json, which is neither. The Backups restore toast can be captured and the finding gives no reason why it could not be, so the diff-line route does not apply either. The branch is declared at spec.md:305. The viewer's state lists at spec.md:279-280 cover the Sharing and Across projects pages, not Backups, and no manifest summary.missing entry names it, so it is not a missing-state defect at the capture spec either. This matches the fourth round's ruling. A capture of the restore toast with sharingReset > 0 would close it.

Upheld as advisory, as in every earlier round. The one log:error is Chrome's network log of the 500 the session caused on purpose (a read-only data directory) to produce the declared error state. The page code logs nothing and shows a plain toast.
Upheld as advisory. The copy reads "1 projects" for a count of one, here and in the Backups toast. It follows the spec's template, which has no singular form.
Upheld as advisory. The loader's problems are shown raw: lower case, a raw env key, and problems joined with ' · '. The copy reads as developer text, but it is plain English.
Upheld as advisory. The sharing pill is drawn inside the LINKS cell and hides that cell's "—", where the spec says "after the links cell". This is a placement detail with no headed column of its own.
Advisory, debt outside the change. The existing "Not linked" toast shows error.message to the user.

Upheld as advisory. Nothing catches the new throw before sharingStatus, share status or GET /api/sharing, so a future broken row would fail the whole command. Today it cannot be reached, and it would fail loudly with the project and destination named. Parts 5 and 6 should decide whether one broken row stops the run or only skips that item.

Upheld as advisory. ADR 0025's predicate contract (docs/adr/0025-sharing-policy.md:70-76) still says decide always returns a ruling, and its step 4 still says "or level-local". Add one sentence to the ADR saying decide throws on a hand-built policy whose row reads local with reason allowed. The code sits within its boundary, and no current caller can hit the throw.

Upheld as advisory, carried. Because of the OR in ledgerRecords' filter, the primary key cannot serve the query, so it scans the whole ledger. The ledger is empty in this item; part 6 should bound the query (Q2).
Upheld as advisory, carried. Nothing reads the sharing_changes_at index, yet every policy change pays to write it (Q2).
Upheld as advisory, carried. No retention or erasure is stated for sharing_ledger or sharing_changes. This item writes no ledger row; part 6 must state the retention before it writes (Q5).
Advisory, debt outside the change. A restored store stays in DELETE journal mode (probes/restore-journal-mode.md). The first round's judge already made this its own item.
